verdict.rationale: Carta's own docs show it holds an issuer's cap table: capitalization by share class, stakeholders, option grants (including drafts awaiting board approval), convertible notes, SAFEs and fully diluted percentage calculations. The evidence is almost entirely read-side API and MCP access, not founder-side maintenance of a live record that investors and auditors rely on. Missing for 10: share certificate management, documented founder workflows for maintaining or editing the ledger beyond draft grants, evidence of auditor or investor reliance as a single source of truth, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a founder, I can maintain my full cap table — share classes, certificates, SAFEs, and option grants — as a live single source of truth that investors and auditors rely on

citations.quote: Retrieve an issuer's capitalization table by share class.
Access ownership, stakeholder lists, SAFEs, convertible notes, option grants, 409A valuations, financing history
A draft option grant is an option grant that is either still being finalized or that has not yet received board consent and approval.
A stakeholder is a person or entity that has been issued a security by an issuer and is, therefore, on the issuer's capitalization table.
